title: The trust stack
objective: Stamp a solver-only result as uncertified, cross-check it with a second solver, read a solver-bug replay and a partial certificate, and compare your obligation with Lean's experimental vcgen as a dated twin.

choice.prompt: CL-1.1 reads PROVED [P] · Z3 5.3.1 unsat · uncertified · rlimit N. What does "uncertified" admit?

options.why: Review is not what the qualifier records.

options.text: That it rests on the solver being sound, and no independent certificate was checked.
options.why: The qualifier names the part you are trusting: the solver.

options.text: That the encoding was not checked.
options.why: That is a separate open defeater, "encoding unverified".
A bound would make it MODEL-CHECKED [M].

blocks.md:
Every stamp in this stage rests on five layers, and each fails in its own way.

| Layer | Must get right | Evidence here | Effect on the stamp |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requirement | `Inv` means the rule | true and false scenarios | requirement-fit is never [P] |
| Semantics | the reference semantics | the Lean reference and its goldens | none |
| VC generator | exactly the fragment's steps | replay and equivalence tests | "encoding unverified" stays open |
| Solver and entry path | `unsat` means no model | a second solver; certificates, deferred | "uncertified" |
| Instrument | the tab's Z3 matches the native one | the course's differential tests | the badge |

The solver layer can fail. Z3 issue #11179 reports a wrong answer on a satisfiable input. Run it.
Input 1 of the issue, sent through Z3's SMT-LIB command interpreter after `(push 1)`, as the report does it. The tab runs one Z3 release, and the recorded run holds four.
blocks.direction: Query asserts: a real `y` of at least 1 whose power `(1/2)^y` is below 1/2. `sat` is the truth, because `y = 2` works. The cell prints what the tab's release says. The recorded run holds what older releases said.

code.text:
from z3 import *

issue = """(set-logic ALL)
(declare-const y Real)
(push 1)
(assert (>= y 1))
(assert (< (^ (/ 1 2) y) (/ 1 2)))
(check-sat)"""

# Through the SMT-LIB command interpreter, as the issue reports it.
ctx = Context()
print('command interpreter:', Z3_eval_smtlib2_string(ctx.ref(), issue).strip())

# Pin y = 2: the same assertions are decided, and the model shows the input is satisfiable.
pinned = Solver()
pinned.from_string('(declare-const y Real)(assert (= y 2))(assert (>= y 1))(assert (< (^ (/ 1 2) y) (/ 1 2)))')
print('with y pinned to 2:', pinned.check())

call.prompt: In the recorded run, one release before the one in your tab, through the command interpreter, what does Z3 answer on input 1?

options.why: That is the truth, and this release missed it.
The recorded output is `unsat` on an input that has a solution. A solver can be wrong.
That is the answer of the release in your tab, not the older one.

blocks.after: That release, and two older ones, report no model for input 1, although `y = 2` is a solution. The tab's release says it cannot decide, and through the Python API so does every tested release {{run:RUN-z3-11179}}. The defect is in nonlinear real exponentiation, outside your checker's fragment. What carries over is that an `unsat` names its solver, its version and its entry path, and stays "uncertified" until something independent checks it. This cracks SEAM-7, the assumption that the solver is sound, which CL-1.1 planted.

blocks.md: A second solver is the cheapest independent check. On the Bench, cvc5 1.4.2 reads the same SMT-LIB. It can also emit a certificate, an Alethe proof of its `unsat`, but a certificate can be partial: its proof for S1's guard query has 3 `hole` steps, each marked "untranslated rewrite". Checking certificates is deferred (D-32), so two agreeing solvers raise your confidence and the stamp keeps "uncertified".

Lean's experimental `vcgen` (Lean 4.35.0, recorded 2026-10-24) reads an obligation from the other side. On a shallow contract for `transfer` over plain integers it proves the guarded version, and with the guard weakened it leaves one goal unproved: the sender's new balance is not known to be non-negative {{run:RUN-lean-vcgen}}. On a Mini-Plinth-style command type it does the same once it is given a weakest-precondition instance and one specification per construct {{run:RUN-vcgen-cmd}}. Your checker finds a violating state for the weakened obligation: an unprovable condition and a satisfiable negation are two faces of one obligation. The proofs close with `grind`, so each lists `Classical.choice`, which S2's manual proofs did not {{run:RUN-vcgen-cmd}} {{run:RUN-lean-ledger}}.

choice.prompt: On S1's guard query, Z3 5.3.1 says `unsat` and cvc5 says `unsat`. No certificate was checked, and the premise witness is satisfiable and replays. Complete the stamp: PROVED [P] · Z3 and cvc5 agree · ___

options.why: Agreement is not a checked certificate, and "encoding unverified" stays open.
No certificate was checked, so nothing certifies the result.
Nothing bounded the search. A bound would make the stamp MODEL-CHECKED [M].

choice.prompt: Four things went wrong. Which one sits in the VC-generator layer?

options.text: A solver reports no model for an input that has a solution.
options.why: That is the solver layer, as in SP-4.5.

options.text: An emitted query leaves out the frame for an untouched account.
options.why: The query no longer says what the command does, and both solvers will answer it faithfully.

options.text: `Inv` says `bal ≥ 0`, but the README also forbids holds above the balance.
options.why: That is the requirement layer: the invariant means less than the rule.

options.text: The same query gets one verdict through one entry path and a different one through another.
options.why: That is the solver and its entry path.

notes: RUN-scaffold pins several tools at once, so the top-level engine names the record and the top-level version is the site stack; each configuration carries its own engine, version, binary_sha256 (where a binary ran), argv, inputs, budget, exit code and verdict lines. Named values (values.*) are what copy cites with {{run:RUN-scaffold#values.<name>}}.

Where a configuration ran: npm, node, uv and cargo ran on the host (Linux x86_64, Node 22). The browser configurations ran in the Playwright image of the same version as @playwright/test, which carries Node 24, so the site and instruments suites ran on Node 24 there; the unit tests and the build ran on Node 22 on the host. The Rust crate check, the wasm build and cvc5 ran in ubuntu:24.04; PostgreSQL ran in postgres:18, reached on a loopback port.

Not executed here: the arm64 build of cvc5 (hashed only; no arm64 emulation on this host) and everything on macOS, Windows or Apple silicon. Soufflé ships no arm64 package at all (RUN-souffle-version).

The PostgreSQL entry pins the service image by digest: postgres:18 is a moving tag, and the digest is what the devcontainer compose file must use. It reports PostgreSQL 18.6, the pin of labs/TOOLS.md.

The Rust crates are the candidates labs/TOOLS.md read from the crates.io API on 2026-10-23, pinned with `=` and resolved into the committed Cargo.lock. On Ubuntu 24.04 `cargo check --locked` passes with build-essential and libclang-dev installed (plus curl and ca-certificates, which only rustup needs): pg_query compiles libpg_query with the C compiler and generates its bindings with libclang. bench-rust-host-without-libclang records the same check stopping at pg_query on a host with no libclang, so the Bench image must carry libclang-dev (W0-T05). The recorded run installs nothing else: no clang binary, no protoc, no pkg-config.

The cvc5 Bench binary is the non-GPL static build, so its version string reads 1.4.2 and carries no -modified suffix, unlike the pip wheel of RUN-cvc5-alethe. The two are different builds of the same release: a receipt records the string verbatim.

kit-wasm-roundtrip is the one check that the vendored ABI pair (the host code and the kit crate) still agrees: a module built by the pinned toolchain against the vendored kit, driven by the vendored host code, unedited.

The browser smoke tests are the scaffold's own: a meta CSP present and nothing blocked, no request to another origin, no console error, axe with no violation at 360, 320 and 1280 px, no sideways scroll. GATE-bundle and GATE-a11y proper are built on the shell (W1).
Re-record this run after any change to package.json, a workspace manifest or package-lock.json: the npm-lock configuration lists their SHA-256 values as inputs, and GATE-runs compares them.
duration_s on the record is the sum of the configurations; informational outputs (summaries with durations) are compared on verdict_lines when the run is re-recorded.

interface.vcgen_docstring_opening:
`vcgen` will break down a Hoare triple proof goal like `⦃P⦄ prog ⦃Q⦄` into verification conditions,
provided that all functions used in `prog` have specifications registered with `@[spec]`.

`vcgen` is experimental and subject to change. `set_option experimental.vcgen true` acknowledges
its experimental status and silences the warning that each call reports.

### Program types

`vcgen` works on any program type `Prog` that carries a `Std.WP.WP` interpretation. A monad
is one such program type. An inductive type of commands is another, once its weakest precondition is
defined in terms of an operational semantics.

experimental.vcgen.descr: acknowledge that the `vcgen` tactic is experimental and subject to change; `true` silences the warning that each `vcgen` call reports

experimental.intrinsic.descr: acknowledge that the intrinsic verification syntax (the contract clauses of a `def`, the `assert` element, and the `invariant` and `decreasing` clauses of a loop) is experimental and subject to change; `true` silences the warning that each of these forms reports

warnings_with_options_off: The `vcgen` tactic is an experimental drop-in replacement for `mvcgen` that will eventually replace it; `set_option experimental.vcgen true` acknowledges its experimental status and silences this warning.
The `ensures` clause is part of the experimental intrinsic verification syntax; `set_option experimental.intrinsic true` acknowledges its experimental status and silences this warning.

The `vcgen` tactic is an experimental drop-in replacement for `mvcgen` that will eventually replace it; `set_option experimental.vcgen true` acknowledges its experimental status and silences this warning.
